True in C17; justification line numbers (done on line 16 of fallthrough.c, line 18 of with_break.c) are correct and the passages support sequential execution through the single body statement.
with_break.c adds break on lines 8 and 11; case 3 already breaks and case 4 is last, so no case runs into the next. Justification's diagnostic counts match the recorded gcc-16 output.
Scoped to gcc-16; recorded diagnostics show fallthrough warnings at 7:9 and 9:9 for fallthrough.c and nothing for with_break.c; the man page passage says -Wextra enables -Wimplicit-fallthrough=3.
Maths: with n = 2 into_break.c prints two, not three (fact f.p3.l1 = two). The justification's step 'puts("three") runs' is also false: line 9 is puts("two") and into_break.c has no puts("three").
Scoped to gcc-16; the recorded into_break.c diagnostics hold one warning at 7:9 and none at line 9, where puts("two") runs into case 3 whose only statement is break.

Sources support it: the cited clang diagnostics are not in the job (programs carry only gcc-16 diagnostics), so the claim cannot be checked. It also drops the compiler version that the recorded run had (Apple clang 21.0.0).
